day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the plane and review your Montreal plans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Old Montreal accommodation, then take a self-guided walk through the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal to get your bearings. Stroll along Rue Saint-Paul, admire the Notre-Dame Basilica exterior (free from outside), and soak in the historic architecture. Head to the Old Port waterfront for fresh air and free views of the St. Lawrence River.
day_by_day.evening: Old Montreal Food Crawl — Begin your Montreal food journey with an evening wander through Old Montreal's iconic food spots. Stop at Marché de la Villette for charcuterie, grab a classic Montreal-style bagel from a nearby vendor, and finish with a crepe from a street stall. The cobblestone atmosphere is especially charming at dusk.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a snack at Trudeau Airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick and affordable sandwich or poutine from a casual café near your hotel on arrival — try La Banquise (a short trip away) or a dépanneur snack to keep costs minimal.
meals.dinner: Old Montreal Food Crawl style: assemble a budget meal from street vendors and market stalls along Rue Saint-Paul. Budget ~$15–20 CAD total. Look for classic Quebec tourtière slices or a hearty bowl of soupe aux pois.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin after 13:00 arrival. Keep the afternoon light to recover from travel. Old Montreal is very walkable from your accommodation — no transit needed. July 15 falls during the Montreal Jazz Festival period, so expect lively street energy even on your first evening.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour — Take the metro (Orange Line) north to Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Arrive early (around 9:00) to beat the crowds and enjoy the freshest produce. Sample local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh fruit, and artisan breads. Many vendors offer free tastings. Budget ~$10–15 CAD for samples and small purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plateau-Mont-Royal neighbourhood on foot. Walk along Avenue du Mont-Royal and Rue Saint-Denis, browsing colourful murals, indie boutiques, and vintage shops (window shopping is free!). Rest in Parc Lafontaine — a beautiful and completely free green space popular with locals — and enjoy a picnic with snacks picked up at Jean-Talon Market.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances — Head to the Quartier des Spectacles for the Festival International de Jazz de Montréal. Hundreds of outdoor performances are completely FREE. Grab a spot on Place des Arts esplanade and enjoy world-class jazz, blues, and fusion music under the summer sky. This is a quintessential Montreal experience at zero cost.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh pastry and coffee at a local boulangerie near your Old Montreal hotel. Try Olive et Gourmando on Rue Saint-Paul for a budget-friendly morning bite (~$8–12 CAD).
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch assembled from Jean-Talon Market — fresh baguette, local cheese, cured meats, and seasonal fruit. Budget ~$12–15 CAD for a generous spread.
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and iconic Montreal meal before the Jazz Festival. Try a classic smoked meat sandwich at a no-frills deli near the Quartier des Spectacles, or grab a falafel wrap on Rue Sainte-Catherine. Budget ~$12–16 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Metro Day Pass (~$11 CAD) is worth buying today to cover the Jean-Talon trip and Jazz Festival travel. Jazz Festival outdoor stages are free — no ticket required. Bring a light jacket for the evening as temperatures can dip slightly after sunset even in July.

day_by_day.morning: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Walk — Friday mornings in the Plateau often feature local street markets and neighbourhood festivals in July. Stroll through the Plateau's iconic 'painted staircases' and colourful duplexes, discover street art along Rue Rachel and Avenue du Parc, and check out any local festival programming happening along Avenue du Mont-Royal. Entry to neighbourhood streets and markets is free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Mont Royal Park (free entry) for panoramic views of Montreal's skyline. The walk up takes about 30–45 minutes and is very accessible. Visit the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for the best city views. Pack a picnic or grab food from a nearby food truck at the base of the mountain. This is a beloved local tradition on warm summer afternoons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Montreal Jazz Festival for another evening of free outdoor performances. Friday nights typically feature larger headline acts on the outdoor stages. Arrive early to claim a good viewing spot. Explore the festival's food vendors for affordable bites and enjoy the electric atmosphere of one of the world's greatest music festivals.

meals.breakfast: Try a classic Montreal bagel with cream cheese from a nearby café or bakery. St-Viateur and Fairmount bagels are legendary — pick one up for ~$2–4 CAD each.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Mont Royal — pick up supplies from a Plateau dépanneur or grocery store (IGA or Metro supermarket) for sandwiches, snacks, and drinks. Budget ~$10–12 CAD.
meals.dinner: Festival food stalls at the Jazz Festival offer affordable options. Look for poutine, grilled corn, or Quebec-style hot dogs (steamés). Budget ~$12–18 CAD. Alternatively, grab a hearty bowl of Vietnamese pho on nearby Rue Saint-Denis for ~$14 CAD.

day_by_day.notes: Mont Royal Park is entirely free and one of Montreal's top attractions. Wear comfortable walking shoes for both the Plateau walk and the mountain hike. The Jazz Festival Friday evening programming is often the most vibrant of the week — don't miss it. Stay hydrated as July afternoons can be warm at 25°C.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Old Montreal for a leisurely Saturday morning exploration. Visit the Marché Bonsecours (exterior and ground floor are free to browse) and walk along the Old Port boardwalk. Rent a BIXI bike (Montreal's public bike share, ~$7 CAD for a day pass) to cover more ground along the waterfront bike path — a fun and budget-friendly way to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mile End neighbourhood, known as Montreal's creative and culinary hub. Visit the famous Wilensky's Light Lunch (a Montreal institution since 1932) and browse the independent bookshops and record stores along Rue Bernard. Catch any remaining Jazz Festival afternoon programming or check local listings for neighbourhood street festivals happening on this Saturday.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening celebration — head back to the Jazz Festival for one last night of free outdoor music. Saturday nights feature some of the festival's biggest performances. Treat yourself to a slightly more indulgent dinner nearby to celebrate your Montreal trip before heading home.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a full sit-down breakfast at a local Old Montreal café. Try Crew Café or a similar spot for eggs, toast, and coffee for ~$10–14 CAD — a relaxed Saturday morning treat.
meals.lunch: Wilensky's Light Lunch in Mile End — a Montreal institution serving their famous pressed salami and bologna sandwiches for under $8 CAD. Cash only, utterly authentic.
meals.dinner: Celebrate your last evening with a meal at a BYOB (apportez votre vin) restaurant — Montreal is famous for these affordable gems. Try a casual Lebanese or Italian BYOB on Rue Saint-Denis or Rue Prince-Arthur (many offer fixed-price menus for ~$20–25 CAD). Pick up a bottle of wine from a nearby SAQ for ~$12–15 CAD to keep the total budget-friendly.

day_by_day.notes: BIXI bike share is one of the best budget ways to explore Montreal — the flat Old Port and Mile End routes are ideal for cycling. Saturday is the liveliest Jazz Festival day, so arrive at outdoor stages early for popular acts. Check the official Jazz Festival app or website for the Saturday lineup. If departing on July 19, ensure checkout and packing are done before your final evening out.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight AC lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Check in to your Old Montreal accommodation, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: After settling in, head straight into the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal. Stop at Olive et Gourmando for a late lunch bite, browse the artisan shops along Rue Saint-Paul, and soak in the historic architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier. The crawl is entirely walkable from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances: Make your way to the Quartier des Spectacles (a short taxi or Metro ride from Old Montreal) to catch free outdoor Jazz Fest street performances. The festival runs through mid-July and the evening atmosphere is electric with live music, food stalls, and crowds of locals.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal before landing
meals.lunch: Olive et Gourmando (Old Montreal) — beloved local café known for its pressed sandwiches, house-baked bread, and fresh salads. Budget ~$18–$25 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: Garde Manger (Old Montreal) — Chef Chuck Hughes' beloved bistro serving creative Québécois-inspired dishes in a lively atmosphere. Budget ~$45–$65 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Your hotel is ideally located for Day 1 — the Food Crawl and Jazz Fest are both reachable on foot or by a short ride. Pack a light rain layer just in case of an evening shower. The Jazz Festival street stages are free; no tickets needed.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take the Metro (Orange Line) north to the Jean-Talon Market, one of North America's largest open-air markets. Spend the morning sampling local Quebec cheeses, maple products, fresh pastries, charcuterie, and seasonal summer produce from local farmers. Arrive by 9:00–9:30 AM to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Walk: Head to the vibrant Plateau neighbourhood (a short Metro or bike-share ride from Jean-Talon). Stroll along Avenue du Mont-Royal and Boulevard Saint-Laurent, exploring street murals, indie boutiques, and any active summer street festivals. The area buzzes with local energy throughout July.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Jazz Festival Quartier des Spectacles for an indoor ticketed concert or continue enjoying the free outdoor stages. Alternatively, wind down with a walk along the Old Port waterfront near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Au Kouign Amann (Plateau) — a beloved local bakery famous for its Breton butter cake and morning pastries. Budget ~$10–$15 CAD per person.
meals.lunch: Eat at Jean-Talon Market itself — graze on market samples and grab a full plate from one of the market's prepared food vendors (charcuterie, fresh bread, local cheeses). Budget ~$15–$20 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: L'Express (Plateau-Mont-Royal) — a classic Montreal French bistro institution open since 1980. Known for steak tartare, duck confit, and an excellent wine list. Budget ~$45–$60 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover a lot of ground between Jean-Talon and the Plateau. Bixi bike-share is a fun and affordable way to get between neighbourhoods on a warm summer day. Check the Jazz Festival schedule in advance to book any ticketed evening shows you want.

day_by_day.morning: Schwartz's Deli & Mile End Bagel Experience: Head to the Mile End neighbourhood for an iconic Montreal food morning. Start with a fresh wood-fired bagel (sesame or poppy) with cream cheese and lox at St-Viateur Bagel or Fairmount Bagel (both legendary, both open early). Then walk a few blocks to Schwartz's Deli on Boulevard Saint-Laurent for a mid-morning smoked meat sandwich — arrive before the lunch rush to avoid long lines.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mont Royal Park: Take a leisurely hike or walk up to the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout for panoramic views over Montreal. The park is green, shaded, and perfect in summer heat. Rent a paddleboat on Beaver Lake or simply relax on the grass with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival — Final Evening: Head back to the Quartier des Spectacles for a festive Friday night. Friday evenings at the Jazz Fest are among the most lively, with major free outdoor headliners and a buzzing street party atmosphere. Grab food from the festival vendors and enjoy the music under the summer sky.

meals.breakfast: St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End) — a Montreal institution. Fresh bagels with cream cheese and smoked salmon. Budget ~$8–$12 CAD per person.
meals.lunch: Schwartz's Hebrew Delicatessen (Mile End/Plateau) — the legendary smoked meat sandwich with mustard on rye, a pickle, and a cherry cola. Budget ~$18–$25 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: Festival street food at Quartier des Spectacles — poutine, crêpes, grilled corn, and local snacks from vendors. Budget ~$20–$30 CAD per person for a relaxed, festive meal.

day_by_day.notes: Schwartz's is cash-preferred and lines can be long — arrive before noon or after 2 PM. Mont Royal Park is a 20-minute bus ride from Old Montreal or a scenic 30-minute bike ride via Bixi. Friday night Jazz Fest crowds are large; arrive early to secure a good spot near the main outdoor stages.

day_by_day.morning: Old Montreal Morning Stroll & Basilica Visit: Spend a relaxed final morning exploring Old Montreal at a slower pace. Visit the stunning Notre-Dame Basilica (book tickets online in advance, ~$15 CAD), walk along the Old Port promenade, and browse the weekend artisan market at Place Jacques-Cartier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Chinatown & Downtown Exploration: Walk or Metro to Montreal's compact Chinatown for a dim sum lunch, then explore the downtown core — window-shop on Rue Sainte-Catherine, visit the McGill campus, or pop into the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (free on Saturday afternoons for Quebec residents; ~$24 CAD for visitors) for a cultural afternoon in the air conditioning.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Old Montreal: End your trip with a memorable dinner back in your neighbourhood. Linger over a long meal, explore the illuminated Old Port at night, and raise a glass of local Quebec craft beer or cider to a wonderful Montreal trip.

meals.breakfast: Crew Collective & Café (Old Montreal) — a breathtaking café inside a former Royal Bank building with soaring ceilings. Great coffee and pastries. Budget ~$10–$15 CAD per person.
meals.lunch: Qing Hua Dumpling (Chinatown) — beloved local spot famous for hand-made dumplings and noodle soups. Casual, delicious, and affordable. Budget ~$15–$20 CAD per person.
meals.dinner: Brasserie 701 (Old Montreal, Hotel Place d'Armes) — elegant but approachable brasserie with a strong Quebec-sourced menu, excellent cocktails, and a beautiful terrace. Budget ~$50–$70 CAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details and plan accordingly if flying out on July 18 or early July 19. Saturday mornings in Old Montreal are lively — the Notre-Dame Basilica can fill up quickly so booking tickets online the night before is strongly recommended. The Old Port is beautiful at golden hour and after dark — perfect for a final evening walk along the St. Lawrence River.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Montreal-Trudeau Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer by private car service to your hotel in Old Montreal. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll along the cobblestone streets of Old Montreal, admiring the 17th-century architecture of Place Jacques-Cartier and the Basilique Notre-Dame de Montréal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Old Montreal Food Crawl: Begin your Montreal culinary journey with a guided wander through the historic quarter. Stop at the beloved Olive et Gourmando for an artisanal bite, explore local chocolatiers and fromageries, and soak in the atmosphere of Rue Saint-Paul — one of the oldest streets in North America. The warm summer afternoon makes this a perfect introduction to the city's gourmet street culture.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival Street Performances: Head to the Quartier des Spectacles (a short taxi or walk from Old Montreal) for the world-renowned Festival International de Jazz de Montréal. Enjoy free outdoor stage performances under the summer sky, then settle into one of the premium ticketed indoor concerts for a more intimate jazz experience.

meals.lunch: Olive et Gourmando (Old Montreal) — celebrated for its gourmet sandwiches, freshly baked breads, and locally sourced ingredients. A perfect first taste of Montreal.
meals.dinner: Toqué! — Montreal's landmark fine-dining institution on Place Jean-Paul-Riopelle. Chef Normand Laprise's tasting menu showcases the finest Quebec seasonal produce. Reserve well in advance. Pairs perfectly with the Jazz Festival atmosphere nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. The Jazz Festival typically runs late June through early July but verify 2027 dates — if active, this is unmissable. Old Montreal hotel is ideally positioned for both the Food Crawl and the Quartier des Spectacles within walking distance or a short ride.

day_by_day.morning: Jean-Talon Market Food Tour: Take a private car north to the vibrant Jean-Talon Market in Little Italy — one of North America's largest and most celebrated open-air markets. Join a guided premium food tour sampling raw-milk Quebec cheeses, artisanal maple products, heritage-variety fruits, charcuterie, and freshly baked pastries. Meet passionate local producers and learn the story behind Quebec's rich culinary terroir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Schwartz's Deli & Mile End Bagel Experience: Journey into Montreal's legendary Jewish deli culture in the Mile End neighbourhood. Savour the iconic smoked meat sandwich at the historic Schwartz's Charcuterie Hébraïque, then walk to St-Viateur Bagel or Fairmount Bagel to watch hand-rolled, wood-fired Montreal bagels being made fresh. Explore the eclectic boutiques and street art of Mile End at a leisurely luxury pace.
day_by_day.evening: Plateau-Mont-Royal Neighbourhood Festival Walk: As the day cools into a warm summer evening, stroll through the Plateau neighbourhood during one of its vibrant street festivals. Discover local artisan vendors, live music on residential squares, colourful staircases, and the infectious joie de vivre of Montreal's most bohemian district.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Le Cartet (Old Montreal) — a beloved local institution serving beautifully crafted Quebec breakfast and brunch dishes with premium local ingredients.
meals.lunch: Schwartz's Deli (Mile End) — a Montreal rite of passage. Order the medium-fat smoked meat sandwich with a side of coleslaw and a black cherry soda. Simple, legendary, irreplaceable.
meals.dinner: Damas (Mile End / Outremont) — an acclaimed upscale Syrian restaurant celebrated for its refined Middle Eastern cuisine, exceptional wine list, and elegant atmosphere. One of Montreal's most lauded fine-dining experiences outside of French cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Jean-Talon Market is best experienced in the morning when vendors are freshest and crowds are manageable. Pre-book a private or small-group gourmet tour for the most immersive experience. The Mile End and Plateau neighbourhoods are best explored on foot — comfortable premium walking shoes recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Mount Royal Park Morning Retreat: Begin the day with a private guided walk up Mont Royal — the iconic hill at the heart of the city designed by Frederick Law Olmsted. Enjoy panoramic views of the Montreal skyline and the St. Lawrence River from the Kondiaronk Belvedere lookout. The warm morning air and lush summer greenery make this a serene and invigorating luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Golden Square Mile & Musée des Beaux-Arts de Montréal: Descend into the Golden Square Mile, Montreal's historic enclave of Gilded Age mansions. Visit the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Montréal (MBAM), one of Canada's finest art museums, for its world-class permanent collection and special summer exhibitions. Take your time in the contemporary and Quebec art wings. Browse the museum's upscale boutique.
day_by_day.evening: Montreal Jazz Festival — Premium Ticketed Concert: Return to the Quartier des Spectacles for a headline indoor concert at the Jazz Festival. The Friday evening lineup typically features internationally acclaimed artists in intimate, world-class venues such as Salle Wilfrid-Pelletier at Place des Arts. Dress elegantly and arrive early to enjoy the festival atmosphere on the outdoor esplanades.

meals.breakfast: Crew Collective & Café or hotel in-room service — enjoy a relaxed premium breakfast before your morning hike.
meals.lunch: Maison Boulud (Ritz-Carlton Montreal, Golden Square Mile) — Chef Daniel Boulud's Montreal outpost offers an exquisite French-inspired lunch in one of the city's most opulent hotel dining rooms, with a stunning garden terrace perfect for summer.
meals.dinner: Le Mousso (East Montreal) — Chef Antonin Morin-Labrechet's avant-garde tasting menu is widely considered one of the most exciting and creative fine-dining experiences in Canada. An unmissable reservation for serious food lovers. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Mount Royal is free to access; a private guided naturalist or historian guide can be arranged through your hotel concierge for a premium experience. MBAM tickets can be purchased in advance online. Jazz Festival indoor concert tickets should be booked well ahead — Friday headliners sell out quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Old Port & St. Lawrence River Private Cruise: Spend your final morning exploring the Old Port waterfront. Arrange a private luxury yacht or catamaran cruise along the St. Lawrence River for stunning views of the Montreal skyline, Île Sainte-Hélène, and the iconic Jacques Cartier Bridge. Enjoy champagne and local charcuterie on board as you take in the summer scenery from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Atwater Market & Saint-Henri Gourmet Exploration: Visit the beloved Atwater Market near the Lachine Canal for a final taste of Quebec's finest local produce — artisan cheeses, heritage meats, seasonal pastries, and fresh flowers. Walk or rent a premium bike along the scenic Lachine Canal path through the trendy Saint-Henri neighbourhood, stopping at independent boutiques and specialty food shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Jazz Festival Grand Finale: Conclude your Montreal journey with a celebratory dinner followed by one last evening at the Jazz Festival's outdoor stages. The Saturday night festival atmosphere is electric, with the largest crowds, most spectacular free performances, and a joyful energy that perfectly captures the spirit of Montreal in summer.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Olive et Gourmando (revisit) — treat yourself to their legendary pastries and specialty coffee one final time before checkout.
meals.lunch: Nora Gray (Saint-Henri) — a sophisticated Italian-inspired bistro with an exceptional natural wine list and a menu rooted in Quebec seasonal ingredients. Beloved by Montreal's culinary insiders.
meals.dinner: Vin Papillon or Joe Beef (Little Burgundy) — Joe Beef is a Montreal institution offering an indulgent, convivial fine-dining experience celebrating Quebec's culinary abundance with theatrical flair. Alternatively, its sister wine bar Vin Papillon offers a more intimate small-plates experience with a legendary natural wine selection. Both require advance reservations.

day_by_day.notes: If departing on July 18, confirm flight time and arrange a premium private transfer. The Old Port boat cruise should be booked 24–48 hours in advance through your hotel concierge. Saturday at the Jazz Festival is the most festive evening of the week — arrive at the Quartier des Spectacles by 8:00 PM to secure a great viewing spot for the main outdoor stage.
